note_en: 谁也不 / 谁也没 means "nobody, neither of them": 谁也不敢先开口 "neither dared to speak first." Here 谁 is not a question word but means "anyone," and 也 plus a negative turns it into "no one at all." English simply says "nobody" or "neither"; Chinese builds the same meaning from "anyone + also + not," like 什么也没说 "said nothing at all." Notice that the negative must come after 谁也, never before it.

sentences.en: Awkward blind dates arranged by friends and family like this have long been a cliché among young Chinese. Compared with the "hardcore" approach of the "matchmaking corners" in parks, where parents directly swap details of their children's height, salary, and property, slowly breaking the ice over cats seems remarkably gentle.
